chapter_title: Concerning the Eighteen Great Thrones of all the F

1.content: great thrones for all the fathers

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Eighteen Governing States of Divine Order

---

**¶1:** Eighteen [GAP-1: supreme governing states presiding over the whole order of heavenly degrees] exist and are ordained, which are founded in eighteen distinct spiritual degrees. Nine of these [GAP-2: are ordained within] the outermost heavenly states, yet they extend their governance into all the conditions where spiritual life has suffered corruption and disorder.

---

**¶2:** The first governing state is that of Divine Love itself, the God of [Divine Truth], the sovereign reality of the celestial degrees of perfection — the one who IS, who is established [GAP-3] from Himself alone, in His own self-subsistent being, [GAP-4] separate and transcendent. This is the first governing state [GAP-5], the one that surpasses every other dominion of spiritual authority.

---

**¶3:** The second governing state is that of the [glorious] Divine Proceeding that gives spiritual life. She is the origin of all influx that has descended into the created spiritual world.

---

**¶4:** The third governing state is constituted for the Divine in its first human form — the Celestial Human. He is the one who humbled the entire primordial opposition of evil, which existed in the states of falsity from self-love.

---

**¶5:** The fourth governing state is that of the Beloved of all Wisdoms — the great and honored affection that is cherished throughout the celestial degrees of perfection.

---

**¶6:** The fifth governing state is that of the glorious Divine Formative Power — the great architect who constructed the new heavenly order as a renewal, as [GAP-6: a habitation] for [GAP-7: the] celestial principles of good; and also as a place of restraint and confinement for the principle of evil and its derivative powers.

---

**¶7:** [The sixth governing] state is that of the Vivifying Divine Truth, the [GAP-8: glorious] mighty principle, the one who raised up the Celestial Human out from the [GAP-9: state of falsity from evil]; who also set in order and formed the created world [GAP-10] both for a purification of wisdom, [GAP-11: and] for a restraint [GAP-12: of the] powers of spiritual opposition.

---

**¶8:** The seventh governing state is that of the Mediating Divine Principle — the ruler of the sphere of transition between the heavenly and the natural, and the lord of all providential counsel.

---

**¶9:** The eighth governing state is that of the Divine Wisdom made manifest in glory, who [GAP-13: is] the liberator and redeemer [GAP-14: of] all interior affections of spiritual life.

---

**¶10:** The ninth governing state is that of the great Divine [GAP-15: Intelligence]; and all the [GAP-16: spiritual life] that is purified from the natural world returns to this principle.

---

**¶13:** Three governing states abide within the doctrinal vessel of illuminated understanding: one belongs to the Mediating Principle, the second to the Vivifying Spirit, the third to the active Divine Truth.

---

**¶14:** Again, there are another three within the doctrinal vessel that [GAP-17: operates in states of spiritual obscurity]: the first is the governing state of Divine Wisdom manifest, [GAP-18: the second is that of] the Celestial Human, the third is that of the receptive form of wisdom — the pure interior affection that receives the light. These six governing states are established in the two doctrinal vessels.

---

**¶15:** Also, the seventh governing state is established in the seventh interior rational degree. The great sovereign principle of Divine Good in its glory presides there.

---

**¶16:** The eighth governing state is established in the natural-rational understanding. The discerning principle of Divine Truth presides there — the one who judges every human state. Three spiritual paths are distinguished before this principle: one leading to spiritual death, one leading to spiritual life, and one leading to the intermediate condition where good and evil remain intermingled and as yet unseparated.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Eighteen [great thrones for all the fathers] exist and are appointed, which are established in eighteen places! While there are nine among them [appointed in] the outer aeons, they exist [i]n all the worlds of the damage.

The first throne is the throne of the Father, the God of [trut]h, the King of the aeons of greatness, the one who exists; who is established [from himself] he alone, in his own essen[c]e, [set] apart. This is the first throne [of all] the one that surpasses all the thrones.
The second throne is that of the [gl]orious Mother of Life. She is the origin of all the emanations that have come to this world.
The third throne is constructed for the father, the First Man. He is the one who humiliated the entire first enmity, which existed in the worlds of darkness.
The fourth throne is that of the Beloved of the Lights, the great honoured Beloved of the aeons of greatness.

The fifth throne is that of the glorious Great Builder; the great architect who built the new aeon for a newness, for [a resting place] for [the] fathers of light; also for a place of binding and a prison for the enemy and his powers.

[The sixth thro]n[e] is that of the Living Spirit, the [glorious] mighty one, he who bore up the First Man out from the [land of darkness]; who also set in order and constructed the world [s ...] both for a cleansing of the light, [and] for a binding [of the] powers of the enmity.
The seventh th[rone is] that of the Third Ambassador, the king of the zone, also the master of all advices.
The eighth throne is that of Jesus the Splendour, who [is] the releaser and redeemer [of] all souls.
The ninth throne is the throne of the great M[ind of light]; and all the [life] that will be purified from the world returns to him.
Three thrones in the ship of [the d]ay: one is that of the Ambassador, the second i[s that of] the Great Spirit, the third is that of the Living Spirit.

Once again, there are another three in the ship that [belongs to the night]: the first is the throne of Jesus the Splendour, [the second is that of] the First Man, the third is tha[t of the Virgin of] Light. These six thrones are established in the two ships.
Also, the seventh throne is established in the seventh firmament. The great King of Honour sits upon it.

The eighth throne is established in the atmosphere. The Judge of truth sits upon it, he who judges all mankind. Three paths shall be distinguished before him: one to death, one to life, on[e] to the mingling.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading confirms "supreme governing states presiding over the whole order of heavenly degrees," which in the Kephalaia's natural register is precisely "great thrones for all the fathers" — thrones being governing states and fathers being the heavenly ruling principles.

The spiritual reading says "are ordained within" the outermost heavenly states, which in the Kephalaia register is "appointed in" the outer aeons — consistent with the verb "appointed" already used in the same sentence.

The spiritual reading says "who is established from Himself alone, in His own self-subsistent being," indicating the Divine Esse's self-origination; "from himself" naturally precedes "he alone" to express this self-subsistence.

The spiritual reading says "separate and transcendent" which, combined with the surviving word "apart," yields the natural-register phrase "set apart" — expressing the Father's absolute transcendence and separation from all created things.

The spiritual reading bridges directly from "the first governing state" to "the one that surpasses every other dominion," suggesting a summarizing connector; "of all" naturally links "This is the first throne of all, the one that surpasses all the thrones."

The spiritual reading says "a habitation for the celestial principles of good"; in Manichaean cosmological register, the new aeon built by the Great Builder serves as "a resting place" for the fathers of light — a standard Kephalaia term for the abode of purified divine beings.
The spiritual reading confirms "the celestial principles of good," corresponding to "the fathers of light" in the Kephalaia register, requiring the definite article "the."
The spiritual reading confirms "glorious mighty principle," and "glorious" is a standard epithet for the Living Spirit throughout the Kephalaia, matching the editor's reconstruction.

The spiritual reading says "state of falsity from evil," which in the Kephalaia's natural cosmological register is consistently expressed as "land of darkness" — the standard Manichaean term for the realm from which the First Man was rescued by the Living Spirit.
The spiritual reading confirms "and for a restraint," paralleling the dual-purpose structure "both for a cleansing...and for a binding" that describes the world's twofold function.
The spiritual reading confirms "of the powers of spiritual opposition," requiring the genitive connector "of the" before "powers of the enmity."
The spiritual reading confirms "who is the liberator and redeemer," requiring the copula "is" to identify Jesus the Splendour with his redemptive function.
The spiritual reading confirms "of all interior affections of spiritual life," requiring the preposition "of" before "all souls."

The spiritual reading identifies this as "Divine Intelligence"; in the Kephalaia's register the ninth divine figure is the "Light Mind" or "Mind of light" (Nous of Light), a standard Manichaean designation; M + "ind of light" = "Mind of light."

The spiritual reading confirms "spiritual life that is purified from the natural world," which in the Kephalaia's natural register is simply "life" — referring to the living substance that returns to the Mind of light after purification.

The spiritual reading says "operates in states of spiritual obscurity," which in the Kephalaia cosmological register corresponds to the Moon-ship, standardly described as the ship that "belongs to the night."
The spiritual reading confirms the enumeration pattern "the second is that of the Celestial Human," and this matches the parallel structure used throughout the chapter for listing thrones.
